A representative consultation group would give employees a formal way to communicate their concerns about childcare and travel directly to managers before the shift changes are finalised. Representatives can gather views from different employees, so managers are more likely to understand practical problems caused by weekend working.

This two-way communication may improve trust because employees can see that management is listening rather than imposing a decision. Managers may then amend shift patterns, for example by considering employees’ circumstances, which could make the final decision seem fairer. Employees are therefore more likely to accept the changes and cooperate with them, reducing conflict and improving employee relations.

Final inspection identifies faulty containers after production, shortly before dispatch. It can prevent some loose lids or cracked seals from being sent to customers, but it does not stop the defects being made in the first place. Defective containers may already have used materials and labour and may need to be reworked or discarded.

Quality assurance is different because it aims to prevent defects during the production process. Training staff, using standardised machine settings and carrying out checks while containers are being made should reduce the likelihood of loose lids and cracked seals occurring. This should lead to more consistent output and fewer defective containers reaching customers.

As a result, Harbour Homeware may experience fewer returns and online complaints. Customer satisfaction and the business’s reputation could improve, potentially helping it retain customers. The firm could also reduce the cost of waste, rework and handling returned containers, improving efficiency.

However, quality assurance requires staff training and production checks, which may increase costs initially and could slow production while employees adapt to the new procedures. Its success will depend on staff consistently following the settings and checks. Nevertheless, unlike relying only on final inspection, effective quality assurance tackles the causes of defects rather than only detecting them at the end.

Becoming a plc would allow Northton Foods to issue shares to the public and potentially raise substantial finance for the new production site. This may be more suitable than relying on a large long-term loan because share capital does not have to be repaid in the same way as borrowing. The business could use the funds to build the site without creating large loan repayments, which may reduce pressure on cash flow while the new site is being developed.

A successful share issue could also enable the business to raise more finance than the two founders could provide themselves. If the new site increases production capacity successfully, Northton Foods may be better able to meet demand and grow.

However, issuing shares would dilute the founders’ ownership. As public shareholders buy shares, the founders may no longer have the same level of control over decisions. Shareholders may also expect dividends and may judge the directors on the company’s performance, increasing pressure on the founders.

Becoming a plc can therefore provide the substantial, long-term finance needed without a large loan, but it involves giving up some control and taking on obligations to public shareholders. Whether it is preferable depends on whether the founders value retaining control more highly than accessing the finance for the new site.
